citations.quote:
Assume full AC. Let $F_0,F_1\subset S^3$ be compact smooth embedded spanning surfaces for the same nonempty link $L$, with supplied radial collars in disjoint smooth normal tubes of $L$. Orient each component of $L$ arbitrarily, orient the tube boundary tori by their outward normal toward the link exterior, and orient the two surface boundary curves compatibly with $L$. Let $\alpha$ be a smooth proper transverse common arc in the exterior, transverse to its boundary, with transverse boundary-curve crossings at its distinct endpoints. Extend it radially to an isolated smooth embedded arc $A$ ending on $L$. Suppose its two ordered endpoint intersection signs agree, so their sum is $2$ or $-2$.

For every open neighborhood $U$ of $A$ there are a smooth closed ball $B\subset U$ with $A\subset\operatorname{int}B$ and a continuous surjection $q:S^3\to S^3$, fixed off $\operatorname{int}B$, such that its only non-singleton fiber is $A$, $q(B)=B$, and
$$(B,q((F_0\cup F_1)\cap B))\cong(B^3,B^3\cap\{z=0\}).$$
Thus this actual local surface image is a properly embedded locally flat disk, including at the collapsed point. The surfaces may be disconnected or nonorientable. No definiteness or primeness assumption is needed for this local assertion.

Assume full AC. Fix a finite cyclic subdivision of $S^1$ into edges. Let $c:S^1\times(0,1]\to S^2$ be continuous, with each $c_r$ an embedding. On every closed edge require that $c$ extends smoothly to an open neighborhood of that edge times each compact positive-radius interval, and has nonzero edge tangent there. At each subdivision vertex require the two one-sided tangent lines of $c_r$ to be distinct for every $r>0$; the family is smooth away from these finitely many corners. Then
$$D=\{0\}\cup\{r c_r(s):s\in S^1,\ 0<r\le1\}$$
forms a standard ball-disk pair: there is a homeomorphism $(B^3,D)\cong(B^3,B^3\cap\{z=0\})$. In particular it is a properly embedded locally flat closed topological disk. There need be no positive lower bound on corner angles as $r\downarrow0$.

More precisely a radius-preserving homeomorphism of $B^3$ carries $D$ to a disk supplied by a smooth positive-radius family of embedded circles. If the subdivision has no corners and the family is already smooth, this preliminary homeomorphism may be the identity.

Assume full AC. Let $B$ be a smoothly parametrized closed three-ball in a smooth three-manifold. Let $D\subset B$ be a properly embedded locally flat topological disk supplied with a homeomorphism of pairs $(B,D)\cong(B^3,D^2_0)$, where $D^2_0=B^3\cap\{z=0\}$. Suppose $C=\partial D$ is smooth and $D$ is a smooth embedded surface in a neighborhood of $C$, transverse to $\partial B$ there.

There is a smooth properly embedded disk $D'\subset B$, agreeing with $D$ on a smaller boundary collar, and an ambient topological isotopy of $B$, fixed pointwise on $\partial B$, carrying $D$ to $D'$. This isotopy extends by the identity outside $B$. No smoothness or differentiability of the supplied standard-pair homeomorphism is assumed. The assertion requires the actual smooth transverse collar; it does not apply directly to a disk with unrounded corners on its boundary.

derivations.claim: Apply the explicit construction [F1] in a smooth ball $B_{\rm out}\subset U$, and use its adapted diagonal coordinates to identify that ball with $B^3$. The map $q$ is fixed on its boundary and outside it, preserves the ball, and has only $A$ as a nonsingleton fiber, with image at the coordinate origin. In these smooth target coordinates its entire surface image inside the ball is the finite-corner radial disk of [F1]. Choose $r_0=1/2$, and let $B_{\rm in}$ be the coordinate ball of radius $r_0$. Restricting and rescaling the circle family to $0<r\le r_0$ satisfies the same hypotheses in [F2], so the surface image in this inner ball also has an actual standard-pair homeomorphism. These target balls are smooth in the original ambient structure, since the adapted chart and its fixed diagonal rescaling are smooth.

Choose a smooth radial cutoff $\lambda$ equal to one on a neighborhood of $r_0$ and zero outside $(1/3,2/3)$. In each corner box from [F2] replace its displacement $\Delta_r$ by $\lambda(r)\Delta_r$. The resulting fiber derivative in $y$ is $1+\lambda(r)\chi'((y-f_r(x))/a(r))\Delta_r/a(r)>1/2$. Thus it is still an increasing interval homeomorphism, equal to the identity near the box ends. It has a continuous inverse jointly in the parameters by strict monotonicity with this uniform lower slope bound. Outside its horizontal support it is also the identity. Compose these finitely many disjoint corner maps and extend by the identity to obtain sphere homeomorphisms $T_r$. At radii where $\lambda=0$ they are the identity, and near $r_0$ they are exactly the smoothing maps in [F2].

Put $T(r\omega)=rT_r(\omega)$ and take $T$ to be the identity at zero and outside $B^3$. It is an ambient homeomorphism supported in $1/3<r<2/3$, with inverse obtained from $T_r^{-1}$. In particular it preserves every concentric ball and fixes neighborhoods of the center and the outer boundary. Near $r_0$ its surface image is parametrized by $r\gamma_r(s)$ for the jointly smooth embedded-circle family in [F2]. This is a smooth embedded annulus transverse to every radius sphere: its radial derivative has radial component one, whereas its nonzero circle derivative has radial component zero. The parametrization is injective because radius and the circle embedding recover both parameters. Local inverses and compact circle charts give the actual embedded annulus. Thus the transformed disk inside $B_{\rm in}$ has the smooth transverse collar required in [F3], as well as the standard-pair chart obtained by composing the chart from step 1.1 with $T^{-1}$.

Apply [F3] to that inner disk. Extend its boundary-fixed ambient isotopy by the identity outside $B_{\rm in}$, and write $V$ for its endpoint. The new inner disk is smooth and agrees with the previously smooth annulus on a smaller boundary collar. Therefore it joins smoothly to the unchanged exterior annular part across the whole inner boundary circle. Take $H=V\circ T$ in the target chart, extended by the identity outside $B_{\rm out}$. Both factors preserve the inner ball and the outer ball, and $q(A)$ remains inside the inner ball because $T$ fixes the origin and $V$ preserves the ball interior. Since $H$ is a homeomorphism, the fibers of $Hq$ are precisely those of $q$. This proves the asserted local cap and all support and fiber properties. No smoothness outside the specified inner disk and boundary annulus has been inferred.

boundaries.reason: The input is one isolated standard arc with an actual surface pair and boundary collars.

boundaries.evidence: Step 3.1 sets T to the identity near radius zero, leaving the already supplied collapse center well defined.
Step 1.1 treats one actual arc; disjoint finite compositions are separate global uses.
Step 2.1 keeps the fiber derivative greater than one half under the cutoff; corner angle degeneration at zero is irrelevant because support lies between radii one third and two thirds.
Step 3.1 supplies an actual smooth transverse annulus at radius one half; Step 4.1 matches that smaller collar exactly after cap replacement.
The Statement explicitly assumes full AC inherited through the three geometric suppliers; Step 2.1 adds only an explicit cutoff and finite composition.

axioms.use: Full AC is inherited from the actual standard-arc and finite-corner radial constructions and the relative smooth disk replacement. The cutoff of the explicit fiber maps and the finite compositions introduce no further choice.

risk_review.notes: Uses the actual standard-arc radial level construction and the explicit corner fiber formula, each fully archived. It proves only local cap smoothing; no global surface or diagram reconstruction is claimed.

lem-standard-arc-collapse-admits-a-relat.proof_status_evidence: Four actual local proof rows with explicit final scoped checks; independent mathematical review and canonical readiness remain root-owned.
